summary:
Set 128 Session 3 of 3 is the set-terminal session. It re-authored the four UNSTARTED specs so the blocking shape check Session 1 shipped refuses none of them, retired the source-of-record note, and closed the set.

(1) THE DOGFOOD IS MET, ON SPECS THIS SET DID NOT AUTHOR. `spec_admission --all --check` now reports 0 unstarted specs requiring restructuring, down from 4 (113, 118, 121, 122 -- fourteen sessions). The remaining exit-1 is 49 sessions over the step CAP in started/complete sets, explicitly out of scope per this set's spec ("their sessions are closed"), and no CI job invokes the command.

(2) SET 118 WAS RE-AUTHORED SUBSTANTIVELY, AND ITS NUMBERS WERE RE-READ RATHER THAN RESTATED. The counters were VALIDATED FIRST by reproducing 118's own 2026-08-10 row exactly at its own commit (124 files / 3,345 functions / 60,188 test LOC), so the columns are comparable rather than merely adjacent. At HEAD: 133 / 3,513 / 67,182, ratio 0.99, 4,171 collected. Two of the three findings strengthened. The COUPLING figure did NOT reproduce: 43 files / 1,294 tests under 118's literal prose detector, 48 / 1,497 under a bare __file__ reading, bracketing the stated 47 / 1,485 -- the number was always detector-dependent and the detector was never written down. 118's Step 4 now chases a NAMED discrepancy instead of hoping for a match, and its inherited "0.91-1.04" ratio band (unsupported by any row on the page) was corrected to the observed 0.91-1.01 per L-064-8.

(3) THE A4.1 COLLISION -- the finding that made this the substantive half. run_of_record.classify_changed_paths decides "is this a test" BY PATH ALONE: it does not distinguish an edited test from a DELETED one and does not check the path still exists. So a test file deleted after the full suite classifies as test-only, and post_round_delta reports nothing owed -- while 118's own Session 2 rules, under the constitution's hard carve-out, that retiring a test IS a verification reduction. Both statements are correct in their own frame; together they are a hole exactly the shape of 118's deliverable. The verifying critic confirmed the reading independently against the code. Remedy: a hard ordering constraint carried IN THE ATTESTED RECORD -- the retirement pass lands before verification, never after the full suite, and one discovered late is deferred rather than slipped in -- plus an anti-pattern and an end-of-set deliverable. Framed as a constraint on 118, not a defect against 128: A4.1 is sound for the case it was written for, and 118 is simply the first set whose PRODUCT is deletion.

(4) THE SPEC'S OWN PREDICTION WAS RE-MEASURED AND IS 13/14 TRUE. It asserted all fourteen sessions would land at 7 steps / N=3 with no sessionSizeException owed anywhere, and instructed Session 3 to "re-measure rather than trust that sentence". Two sessions had real work compressed into the ceremony step. 113 S4 folded faithfully (follow-on-set reservation into the outcome step, the dogfood UAT into close-out -- both were already bundled with "and close"). 121 S2 did NOT: its step 5 derives the PARAMETERS (N and the cap) that steps 3-4's rules consume, the sequencing note flags both as proposed-not-measured, and it owns progress key numbersDerived. Folding it would have buried a named deliverable in prose -- the exact failure mode the skeleton prevents -- so it declares an exception with its reason, journalled with the two rejected alternatives.

(5) BOTH PATH-AWARE CRITICS INDEPENDENTLY FOUND THE SAME REAL DEFECT IN MY OWN WORK. pull_critique refused (direct-API lane only; this Copilot seat holds no DABBLER_* keys by design), so the sanctioned manual flow ran through route() on the copilot-cli transport -- agentic and path-aware under a read-only tool allowlist (L-125-1) -- gpt-5.5 then gemini-3.1-pro-preview, cheapest premium-weight first, BOTH ON THE SAME TREE so the second was not grading a remediated one. Both found that my new corpus test iterated _discover_specs with no assertion it returned anything: an empty discovery would have passed having examined ZERO specs. That is precisely the L-112-1 vacuous-pass shape this set exists to prevent, and the sibling falsifier could not close it because it plants into tmp_path rather than repo_root. Fixed with a non-empty guard and PROVED by probing _discover_specs to return [] -- both tests then fail -- with spec_admission.py restored byte-for-byte.

(6) THE SET DOGFOODED ITS OWN A4 MACHINERY TWICE, ON TWO DIFFERENT CHANGE CLASSES. After the critique fix, post_round_delta was asked what was owed rather than assumed: shipped-code, A4.2, one delta-scoped remediation-review -- run exactly as prescribed (round 2, VERIFIED, 1 fix accepted). Then the Step 9 guidance edit staled it again, and rather than reverting to duck the gate -- which would have been routing around this set's own control on the set that ships it -- the same arm was paid a second time (round 3, VERIFIED, 1 fix accepted) followed by a full re-run of the suite. The final post_round_delta reads no-change. Session 2's residual said the A4.2 arm had never fired in production; it has now fired twice, on a test-file change and on a config/guidance change.

(7) STEP 9 AMENDED L-112-1 RATHER THAN RATIFYING IT. The lesson was in my preload, I read it, and I still shipped a vacuous scan -- which is evidence its wording did not cover this failure mode, not that the process worked. It now carries an "assert the INPUT SET is non-empty as well as the verdict" clause naming the different-root trap. lessons-learned.md's ceiling was raised 2,385 -> 2,504 strictly TO FIT the measurement under the operator's standing authorization of 2026-08-12, with the reason stated in the config comment per that authorization's second condition; the total stays under its ceiling at 12,118 / 12,200 and guidance_report --check exits 0.

(8) A3 SAVED TWO SUITES AGAIN. run_of_record check reported pytest as the only suite owed -- mocha and playwright report "session touched none of this suite's surfaces" -- because this session changed one test file, one config file and documentation. Final run of record: 4,164 passed / 9 skipped in 723.6s. The count moved 4,162 -> 4,164: the two corpus tests, and nothing else.

residuals.item: The standing operator authorization to exceed the guidance preload ceilings (2026-08-12) is ACTIVE and must be retired. This session used it a second time (lessons-learned.md 2,385 -> 2,504, raise-to-fit with the reason in the config comment).
residuals.note: Recorded in three places so it cannot be lost: the verbatim quote and its three conditions in docs/guidance-lifecycle.md, the matching paragraph beside the ceilings in ai_router/router-config.yaml, and an explicit retirement obligation written into Set 121's own spec. Two sets have now drawn on it, which is the argument for retiring it on schedule rather than letting it become the norm.

residuals.item: A5 -- how 'the required portion' resolves per MODULE -- remains open and is owned by Set 129.
residuals.note: This session retired the source-of-record note to FIXED and marked the A5 heading OWNED rather than leaving it silent. Set 118's re-authoring was also instructed NOT to answer A5 in passing, even where a retirement makes the question tempting.

residuals.item: Set 118's coupling figure is superseded but not yet replaced. The spec now says 47 files / 1,485 tests does not reproduce and brackets it (43/1,294 and 48/1,497), but the authoritative number will not exist until test_inventory publishes its predicate.
residuals.note: Deliberately left as a named discrepancy for that step to chase rather than silently patched here: picking one of the two readings now would invent an authority this session does not have, and the whole point of 118's Step 4 is that the TOOL's answer supersedes the spec's.

residuals.item: The A4.1 test-deletion gap is constrained by process in Set 118, not closed in code. classify_changed_paths still cannot distinguish a deleted test from an edited one.
residuals.owner: Set 118 (its attested record carries the ordering rule)
residuals.note: Deliberate. Making the classifier deletion-aware would change A4's shipped semantics on the set that merely CONSUMES them, and no set other than 118 has deletion as a product. If a second such set ever appears, the constraint should be promoted from 118's attested record into the classifier itself.

residuals.item: The step-checklist gate is recorded as PARTIAL for this session and is NOT waived: one transition (the last-logged-step one close_preflight surfaced) was posted after its window rather than inside it.
residuals.owner: recorded, not owed -- the gate is advisory (Set 116 S3)
residuals.note: One transition left a record with no post inside its own window: the last-logged-step transition flagged by close_preflight, which was posted immediately on being surfaced -- so the post exists but landed after the window rather than inside it. Every other transition this session was posted before the fact (session start, each step transition, before both long-running pytest runs, and before close), and verify_session posted its own three round transitions. The gate is ADVISORY (Set 116 S3 ruling) and is NOT waived here: a waiver needs an operator attestation and none was sought, so the omission is recorded rather than excused. This is the third consecutive session to record the same structural shape, which strengthens the Step 9 observation Sessions 1 and 2 both offered: a sanctioned writer that appends a gate-visible record could post the checklist itself from the line after its append -- run_of_record and session_log here, exactly as verify_session already does for round transitions. Offered again for Set 121, NOT scope taken here.

residuals.item: validate_disposition rejects checklist.status == 'partial', but close_session never calls validate_disposition -- so all three sessions of this set wrote a checklist block the authoring-time validator considers invalid and every one of them closed cleanly.
residuals.owner: unassigned -- surfaced for operator triage, or the next set that touches disposition validation
residuals.note: An L-066-1-shaped parity gap: a validator whose rule nothing on the close path enforces is indistinguishable from no rule, and the disposition authored by every session in this repo is the artifact it governs. Either close_session should call it (and 'partial' should become legal, since a non-waived partial is a real and honest state) or the rule should be dropped. NOT fixed here: it is unrelated to this set's scope, and changing close-path validation at the close of a set is exactly the kind of late shipped-code edit A4.2 exists to make expensive. This session complied with the validator's stated contract by omitting the block.
